Elena — thanks for the questions and for the excellent session yesterday. High level proposal (ballpark numbers so your team can model):

Conversion credits (recommended approach)
- Structure: credit applied as a dollar credit against the first 6 invoice cycles and monthly true-up thereafter. This keeps accounting simple for both sides.
- Typical size: 3 months of your historical hosted spend (based on trailing 3 months) as a conversion credit that reduces the committed spend requirement on a pro-rata basis.

Bridge months
- Option A (standard): 2 bridge months at 50% off reserved rate while we stand up the pool and migrate live traffic.
- Option B (enterprise): 1 full free bridge month + 1 month at 25% off for customers committing >$500k ARR to Dedicated.

Commit offsets / example numbers
- Example starting commit: $200k / month reserved capacity (12-month term) — conversion credit of ~$600k applied across first 6 months (i.e., $100k/month offset).
- If you prefer a shorter term, we can do a 6-month reserve with higher per-month pricing and correspondingly smaller conversion credit.

GPU pool sizing (quick sketch)
- For 120 r/s bursts, 600 token average response: recommend initial pool of 4 x A100-80GB (or equivalent 48GB q8 configs) with autoscaling headroom to +2 nodes for peaks.
- Expected steady throughput: ~80–100 r/s at 512-token latency targets with 95th percentile tail designed for sub-400ms for 512 tokens (depends on model choice / quantization).
- We provide an SLO commitment on sustained throughput per the committed capacity; fallback routing to Hosted is available for overflow.

Operational notes
- We can stage a canary traffic shift and maintain a temporary Hosted fallback for the first 30 days.
- Suggested rollout: week 0 provision + validation, weeks 1–2 canary (10–30% traffic), week 3 full cutover.

I'll drop the sizing sketch and a simple credit model spreadsheet (attached) — happy to run numbers against your actual hosted spend. If this direction looks like a fit, Ben can draft the commercial outline and Karthik will help size the SLA language.

Best,

Elena — quick follow from me on the commercial packaging: 

- Discount tiers: 10% off list reserved rates for 12-mo $200k+/month, 15% for $400k+/month. We can layer an additional 3–5% on conversion if you sign within 30 days.
- Commit true-up: quarterly true-up with a 10% threshold for shortfall; if actual usage is >120% of committed, overage billed at a blended deviance rate.
- Contract language: conversion credits applied to committed ARR (not to overage charges) and will be reflected in the first 6 invoices. We can make credits refundable only as an accounting credit (non-cash) to keep alignment.

Alternative (procurement preference): instead of up-front conversion credit, we can provide a time-limited 'usage credit' pool that offsets Hosted invoice lines for the first 90 days. This sometimes simplifies procurement approvals.

If useful, I can sketch two commercial options (Preferred commit vs Short-term onramp) and send a side-by-side comparison. When can we get a procurement contact and target signing window?
